title: Additive effects of the biopesticide azadirachtin combined with linalool on the life table parameters and behaviour of Drosophila melanogaster
content:
Azadirachtin combined with linalool at a 3:1 ratio exhibited an additive effect at both LD25 and LD50 levels and was significantly more effective than azadirachtin alone in reducing fly growth and reproduction, as well as enhancing behavioural repellency. These findings provide valuable experimental evidence for further evaluation of the additive azadirachtin–linalool combination against other agriculturally important pest species.


Abstract

Excessive use of insecticides contributes to environmental pollution, degrades soil quality, and promotes the development of resistance in insect pests. Botanical compounds are considered effective, safe, and eco-friendly alternatives to synthetic products for the management of insect pests and vectors. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of azadirachtin, applied individually or in combination with linalool at sublethal and lethal doses (LD25 and LD50), on the life table and behaviour of Drosophila melanogaster larvae. Results showed that the bioinsecticide activity of the mixture applied at a 3:1 ratio and tested at both the LD25 and LD50 levels exhibited an additive effect on larval mortality. The results showed that azadirachtin, when applied individually, significantly inhibited the growth rate, reduced fecundity, and altered oviposition and larval preference, indicating a marked repellent effect. Binary combinations of azadirachtin with linalool were more effective than azadirachtin alone, leading to greater reductions in growth rate and fecundity, as well as enhanced repellency. Females exhibited increased oviposition aversion in azadirachtin–linalool-treated mediums, showing a clear preference for untreated zones. Larvae also exhibited significant repellency to the azadirachtin–linalool arenas, remaining predominantly in untreated arenas rather than moving to treated ones. These results suggest that azadirachtin combined with linalool at a 3:1 ratio may serve as an effective strategy for controlling insect populations while simultaneously reducing reliance on the inappropriate and excessive use of harmful chemical insecticides.
